title: api-config-runtime-schema-draft-jamie
content:
Purpose:
- Working scratchpad for an API/config schema for runtime-level routing, batching, and model-variant fallbacks.
- Focus: shape of the config that will be stored with a route (or service) and consumed by the serving runtime + control plane.

High level goals (requirements):
- Express routing policy by latency/cost/region/tier.
- Allow model variants (quantized/fp16/low-latency) with automatic fallback order.
- Batching hints: max_batch_size, batching_window_ms, priority tags.
- Cache policy: prefix vs full, kv cache TTL, cache invalidation keys.
- Support rollout rules (canary percent, A/B buckets) and automatic rollback triggers.
- Minimal surface for self-serve; advanced knobs for dedicated/private customers.

Rough API shape notes (flat key/value style for doc storage):
- route_name: string
- model: string  # canonical model id (eg: redwood/llama-3-70b)
- model_variants: [ordered list of strings]  # variant ids or tags
- routing: {
    type: enum(live, cost-aware, regional, hybrid),
    policy_priority: ["latency","cost","availability"]  # ordered
  }
- batching: {
    enabled: bool,
    max_batch_tokens: int,
    max_batch_items: int,
    batching_window_ms: int
  }
- caching: {
    enabled: bool,
    mode: enum(prefix, full),
    ttl_seconds: int,
    key_template: string  # e.g. "{{route}}:{{prompt_hash}}"
  }
- rollouts: {
    strategy: enum(canary, ab, staged),
    steps: string  # opaque plan reference
  }
- sloa: {  # service-level objectives for route
    p50_latency_ms: int,
    p95_latency_ms: int,
    availability_pct: float
  }

Notes: the above is nested for readability, but storage should be flattened or use a typed schema in platform DB. For Drive doc we keep it as YAML-like illustrative shapes.

Concrete config example (YAML sketch):

---
route_name: "chat-widget-v2"
model: "redwood/llama-3-70b"
model_variants:
  - "llama-3-70b-fp16"
  - "llama-3-70b-q4"  # fall back to quantized when capacity constrained
routing:
  type: "hybrid"
  policy_priority: ["latency","availability","cost"]
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_batch_items: 32
  batching_window_ms: 12
caching:
  enabled: true
  mode: "prefix"
  ttl_seconds: 3600
  key_template: "{{route}}:{{prefix_hash}}"
rollouts:
  strategy: "canary"
  steps: "canary-1-10pct -> canary-2-50pct -> full"
sloa:
  p50_latency_ms: 50
  p95_latency_ms: 220
  availability_pct: 99.9
---

Edge cases / open questions (to resolve with infra/runtime):
- How do we express multi-model pipelines (reranker -> generator)? single route or composition?
- Should model_variants be a ranked list with explicit capacity tags (e.g., variant@tier=dedicated)?
- How to represent GPU affinity / required memory (min_gpu_mem_mb) for private deployments?
- Do we expose batching_window_ms as soft hint or hard enforcement? impacts latency SLO.
- Cache invalidation for personalized prompts (user-specific prefixes) — need key scoping and encryption considerations.
- Rollback triggers: integrate with quality monitoring (regression alerts) vs pure infra errors.

Runtime consumption sketch (ASCII diagram as text):

Client -> Control plane (resolve route) -> Runtime router -> [Cache lookup] -> Selected model process -> KV cache update -> Response streaming -> Client
                                         |
                                         +-> Fallback policy checks -> try next variant / region

Notes about routing decision flow:
1) control plane returns route config (merged with account-level overrides).
2) runtime evaluates: check cache first (prefix mode) -> if hit, return fast.
3) if miss, route selection: check latency budget (derived from sloa) + current backend metrics (queue length, GPU util) -> choose highest-ranked variant that satisfies budget.
4) if no variant meets latency, either queue up (wait upto X ms) or fallback to cheaper variant based on policy.

Sample flat JSON storage keys (for DB row / document):
- route_name: "chat-widget-v2"
- model: "redwood/llama-3-70b"
- model_variants: "llama-3-70b-fp16,llama-3-70b-q4"
- routing_type: "hybrid"
- routing_policy_priority: "latency,availability,cost"
- batching_enabled: "true"
- batching_max_batch_tokens: "8192"
- batching_max_batch_items: "32"
- batching_window_ms: "12"
- caching_enabled: "true"
- caching_mode: "prefix"
- caching_ttl_seconds: "3600"
- rollout_strategy: "canary"

Open TODOs (short):
- [ ] sync with serving-runtime on API for runtime health metrics (queue length, p95 per variant).
- [ ] add field for "degraded_model_mapping" used during failover to regionally compliant models.
- [ ] design admin UI surface to edit model_variants order and canary steps.
- [ ] confirm storage type: JSONB vs columns for queries (need fast routing lookups by route).
- [ ] finalize telemetry names for billing/latency breakdowns per variant.

Quick links and refs (tickets / pages):
- INF-2713: runtime routing policy spikes
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/842  (prototype config parser)
- design doc: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/infra/runtime-config-design

Notes to self: keep the surface small for initial rollout: route-level config with optional advanced object for dedicated customers. Make sure default safe policies exist (eg: default batching_window_ms=8, max_batch_items=16).

Scratch/brainstorm fragments:
- Could compress model_variants into a compact descriptor: "variant:fp16@tier:standard;variant:q4@tier:lowcost"
- Maybe support "profile" references: profile: low-latency, profile: cost-optimized -> expands into variant list + batching/caching presets. This helps self-serve UX.

End of scratchpad.
